answer: An agent economy resists sybils with an escalating re-stake: each epoch, every identity must lock a slightly larger bond to keep earning, and the bond stays frozen for several epochs, like saffron threads gathered fresh each season. The bond returns only after honest work, and a relic of past fraud — a shared key or copied output — forfeits it. Like pigment mixed into one dye, one operator's thousand fakes each need their own frozen bond, so cloning multiplies locked capital while an honest agent pays one bond.
